claims.text: FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt prepared by arc melting are homogeneous, nearly equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt form face-centered-cubic solid solutions.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt exhibit soft ferromagnetism and low coercivity.
A nearly equiatomic FeCoNiIr alloy satisfies the stated high-entropy criterion of configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Ir is a strongly spin-orbit-coupled element.
Introducing Ir into nearly equiatomic FeCoNiIr will increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Ir addition may produce finer microstructural features.
The Ir-induced changes will enhance domain-wall pinning.
Controlled arc melting, homogenization at 1000–1100 °C, and rapid quenching can retain single-phase fcc FeCoNiIr without secondary phases.
Coercivity in high-entropy fcc alloys of this class is largely controlled by magnetocrystalline anisotropy through its effect on domain-wall motion.
The strong spin-orbit coupling of Ir increases local anisotropic energy barriers.
Increased local anisotropic energy barriers hinder domain-wall propagation.
Hindered domain-wall propagation increases the coercive field.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNiIr will have significantly greater room-temperature coercivity than comparably processed FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt.
The coercivity enhancement will be moderate but significant.
Phase segregation or excessive grain growth may negate the proposed coercivity enhancement.
Lattice distortion may adversely offset the anisotropy-driven coercivity enhancement.

contradictions.description: The boundary limits the prediction to material that remains single-phase fcc, whereas the falsification rule treats detection of a secondary phase or inhomogeneity as falsifying the coercivity mechanism. Such a sample instead falls outside the stated applicability conditions and does not by itself decisively test the conditional hypothesis.
